records.title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to creating a SNAP anti-fraud officer and fraud awareness campaign
records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is estimated that there would be no impact on revenues resulting from the enactment of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council estimates that there would be no additional resources required to fulfill the requirements of this legislation. The legislation would be enacted using existing resources within DSS’s Investigations and Revenue Administration and Food Stamp Operations budget program areas, both of which have adequate resources already budgeted for staffing and operational expenses related to the administration of SNAP and the investigation of fraud related to SNAP. The program areas currently have a vacancy rate of 26.0 and 5.6 percent, respectively, as of February 2026.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget did not provide an estimate.
records.estimate_prepared_by:
Elisabeth Childers-Garcia, Financial Analyst
					
Estimate Reviewed By:		Julia K. Haramis, Assistant Director

records.title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to wellness checks on older adults during certain weather events
records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues resulting from the enactment of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council cannot estimate the potential impact on DFTA or NYCEM’s expenditures resulting from the enactment of this legislation as the actual fiscal impact would depend on any new suitable protocol developed by the agencies, which are unknown at this time.  In addition, existing programs may possibly be used to enact some or part of the requirements of this legislation, including DFTA’s contracted case management agencies, home-delivered meal providers, and other programs that conduct regular phone and in-person check-ins with older adults. Additionally, the New York Police Department also conducts wellness checks through the use of their older adult liaisons which are assigned at each police precinct.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) did not provide an estimate.
records.estimate_prepared_by:
Saiyemul Hamid, Senior Financial Analyst 

Estimate Reviewed By: 		Julia K. Haramis, Assistance Director

records.title: Resolution approving a modification (MN-6) pursuant to section 107(e) of the Charter of the City of New York
records.impact_narrative_revenue:
This legislation recognizes $3.1 billion in greater than projected City funds revenues in Fiscal 2026. This is primarily driven by increases of $1.6 billion from the personal income and pass-through entity taxes and $310 million from the general sales tax. This was partially offset by a $335 million decrease in the business corporation tax. 
 
In addition, miscellaneous revenues increased by $56 million since the last revenue modification, including $30 million in fines and forfeitures and $47 million in miscellaneous revenue. This was partially offset by a $22 million decline in rental income. Unrestricted aid increased by $500 million.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure:
